note: D8's sanctions case. The blocked address is REAL: it is on OFAC's SDN list, and it is the only thing in fixtures/demo/ that is not invented. It is here so that services/compliance can be shown blocking a payout against the list anyone can re-download. A match blocks a payout and keeps the money claimable; it is not a seizure, not a report and not a judgement about a person (SDD §3.20).

control.why: A deliberately unlistable string, so the pass side of the demo cannot name anybody's wallet.

list.redirects_to: a signed wc2h-sls-prod-public-published.s3.us-gov-west-1.amazonaws.com URL, so the client has to follow redirects

verified.how: services/compliance/src/sdn.ts parseSdn() over the retrieved file, then isListed() for each address above, on 2026-11-14
verified.caveat: `sha256` and `digital_currency_addresses` are that day's file. Treasury republishes the list, so a later download has a different version hash and may hold more addresses; the designation itself is what the demo depends on, and it is checked against the live list at run time.
